narrative.overview:
The interface should feel like a capable work surface where learners inspect, assemble, explain, and revise systems. Its visual character is restrained and precise so the architecture, evidence, decisions, and feedback remain the focus. Engagement comes from responsive state changes and meaningful consequences, not decorative spectacle.

The system uses dense but legible controls, cool neutral working surfaces, and one disciplined indigo action color. It explicitly rejects the feel of a passive video course, a generic chatbot, an exam portal, and an overloaded enterprise dashboard. Progressive disclosure must keep one primary task dominant while contextual tools remain close at hand.
keyCharacteristics: Clear hierarchy built from typography, spacing, and tonal layers.
Indigo reserved for action, selection, and progress.
Semantic colors used only when they carry operational meaning.
Familiar product patterns that disappear into the engineering task.

rules.name: The One Action Voice Rule
rules.body: Workshop Indigo is reserved for primary actions, current selection, focus, and progress. It is never background decoration.

rules.name: The Semantic Evidence Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red, blue, violet, and cyan must communicate a named mode, state, category, or consequence. Never scatter them for visual variety.

rules.name: The Contrast Before Quiet Rule
rules.body: Supporting copy must remain readable at WCAG 2.2 AA. If text feels faint, darken it before adding weight or size.

rules.name: The Product Scale Rule
rules.body: Mission workspaces use a fixed, compact type scale. Large display typography belongs only to the Home introduction, never inside panels or task cards.

rules.name: The Evidence Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace means measured or structured data. Do not use it as a general technical aesthetic.

rules.name: The Rare Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked labels identify a small number of system categories. Do not place an eyebrow above every section.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface that already has a visible border does not receive a broad decorative shadow. Elevation appears because state or stacking changed.

rules.name: The Quiet Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadow color is tinted Deep Ink at low opacity. Pure black and hard-edged shadows are prohibited.

dos: Do keep one primary task dominant and reveal contextual tools progressively.
Do reserve Workshop Indigo for actions, selection, progress, and focus.
Do use borders and tonal layers before introducing elevation.
Do provide default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, and error states for every interactive component.
Do preserve stable dimensions for nodes, toolbars, buttons, counters, and timers.
Do pair every semantic color with text, iconography, shape, or position.
Do honor reduced motion and remove mandatory timers when accessibility settings require it.
donts: Don't make the product feel like a passive video course; every learning surface must lead to an attempt or decision.
Don't make the product feel like a generic chatbot; conversation is always grounded in a mission stage and learner evidence.
Don't make the product feel like an exam portal; pressure belongs only to explicitly selected Interview mode.
Don't make the product feel like an overloaded enterprise dashboard; never expose every tool, metric, and panel simultaneously.
Don't nest cards, use colored side-stripe borders, apply gradient text, or add decorative glass effects.
Don't combine a visible one-pixel card border with a broad decorative shadow at rest.
Don't use tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows as default section scaffolding.
Don't exceed the surface radius for cards, panels, or inputs, and never use pill shapes for ordinary containers.
Don't animate decoration. Motion must communicate state, feedback, navigation, or stacking.
